whats_new.title: What's new — 31 July 2026
whats_new.lead_html: Last time there were no new screens. This time there are two: activity over time, split by repository in Git output, and a searchable catalog of every metric we report. The new dashboards are also what you see by default now — and the numbers behind them count the right things across Git, collaboration and AI.

stamp.focus: new dashboards by default & numbers you can check

whats_new.in_short_html: In short: the new metrics UI is on for everyone, Git output gains an activity-over-time table and chart you can download, a new Metric catalog explains every metric and when it last saw data, and lines of code, collaboration and AI cost now count the right things.

new_ui_default.title: The new dashboards are now the default
new_ui_default.description_html: Every page opens on the new metric cards, drill-downs and peer comparisons — no switch to find first. Task delivery, Collaboration, Wiki and Team views moved onto the same engine as Git and AI, so all of them now offer trends, distributions and per-person spread. The previous view is still one toggle away in the sidebar.

activity_over_time.title: Activity over time, by repository
activity_over_time.description_html: A new table and chart in Git output: commits, merged pull requests and lines, split by repository and grouped by day, week or month to match the period you picked. The 10 busiest repositories are listed, the rest roll up into “Other”, and the totals always add up. Switch between chart and table, and download it as CSV or Excel.

vendored_loc.title: Lines of code that count only your code
vendored_loc.description_html: Dependency folders, build output, lockfiles and minified files are recognised and left out of authored line counts. Previously one commit bringing in a vendored tree could add hundreds of thousands of lines to a single person and skew every cohort they sit in — so expect some line counts to settle at their true value. Nothing is hidden: a second view breaks lines down by category, so you can see exactly what was excluded. One gap remains here: GitLab repositories still report 0 lines.

metric_catalog.title: Every metric, defined in one place
metric_catalog.description_html: A new Metric catalog page in the sidebar: search any metric and see what it means, how it's formatted, whether higher or lower is better, which breakdowns it supports — and the last date it saw any data, so an empty chart is explainable rather than mysterious.

ai_cost.title: AI cost, complete, to the day — Cursor included
ai_cost.description_html: Cursor spend used to be empty; it is now filled from priced usage events. Claude usage is collected in full across the period and lands on the day it happened. The metric now states plainly what it measures: usage priced at the vendor's rates, not an invoiced amount.

collaboration_licences.title: Collaboration counted across the right people
collaboration_licences.description_html: Collaboration figures now cover only colleagues who can actually take part. Accounts without a Teams licence are recognised and left out, instead of counting as people who never collaborate and pulling averages down.

honest_no_data.title: “No data” instead of a misleading zero
honest_no_data.description_html: The single metrics engine we promised last time is now in place for collaboration, task delivery and wiki as well. Where something isn't measured yet, you'll see “no data” rather than a zero that looks like a real result.

steadier_data.title: Steadier data across your connectors
steadier_data.description_html: A large round of reliability work — data collection across Jira, Bitbucket, Zoom, Claude and Microsoft 365, data preparation, and first-time setup — so syncs finish, survive rate limits and interruptions, and pick up where they left off. Freshly set-up environments no longer start with blank Jira metrics.

drill_down.title: Trace any number to its evidence
drill_down.description: Today a drill-down shows trends, distributions and per-person spread, but not the underlying records. In flight: open a metric and see the actual commits, pull requests and tasks behind it, with a link straight to the source.

people_matching.title: Better people matching
people_matching.description: Today work by someone whose email doesn't match isn't attributed, which can leave some Git and Jira metrics incomplete. In flight: attributing work to the right person even across multiple, changed or missing email addresses.

role_cohorts.title: Compare like with like
role_cohorts.description: Today a person is compared against their whole department. Planned: peer comparisons against people whose role is expected to do the same kind of work.

release_2026_07_13.title: What's new — 13 July 2026
release_2026_07_13.lead_html: This update makes your dashboards more complete and more accurate. Data now flows and is attributed to the right people across Git, Jira, collaboration and Zoom, and several metrics that were showing wrong or empty values have been corrected. No new screens this time — everything below improves what you already use.

direct_reports_toggle.title: “Direct reports only” toggle is back
direct_reports_toggle.description_html: Filter a team down to just your direct reports — members, heatmap and metrics all update together. On by default, and hidden automatically for teams without sub-teams, where it had no effect.

member_expand_full_metrics.title: Full metrics when you expand a team member
member_expand_full_metrics.description_html: Expanding a person now opens their complete metric set instead of a trimmed subset — so you can assess someone without switching screens.

bitbucket_prs.title: Bitbucket pull requests now counted
bitbucket_prs.description_html: Pull-request activity from Bitbucket is attributed to the right person. Review metrics that used to show zero now reflect real work.

consistent_git_metrics.title: Consistent commit & lines-of-code metrics
consistent_git_metrics.description_html: Commit and LOC figures now come from a single shared source, so Git activity is reported the same way across connectors.

readable_git_charts.title: Readable quarterly & yearly Git charts
readable_git_charts.description_html: Long-range charts no longer repeat the same label over and over. Quarterly and annual trends are now legible.

jira_task_delivery.title: Jira Task Delivery metrics now populate
jira_task_delivery.description_html: Closed tasks are detected by their status category rather than English-only status names, so non-English and custom “Done” workflows report correctly.

zoom_data.title: Zoom meeting data restored
zoom_data.description_html: The Zoom sync was hitting an API limit and stalled for about ten days. It's fixed, so meeting activity repopulates going forward.

ai_adoption_graphs.title: AI adoption graphs fixed
ai_adoption_graphs.description_html: AI-adoption graphs now show real distributions with honest “no data” states instead of blanks or misleading zeros.

claude_code_cost.title: Claude Code cost shown as currency
claude_code_cost.description_html: The “Claude Code Cost” metric now displays as money instead of a raw number of cents — no more figures that looked inflated.
